Abstract.AbstractText: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a plant pathogen that causes crown-gall disease. This pathogen is capable of transferring the T-DNA from its Ti-plasmid to the host cell then integrating it into the host genome. To date, this genetic transformation ability has been harnessed as a dominant technology to produce genetically modified plants for both basic research and crop biotechnological applications. However, little is known about the interaction between Agrobacterium and host plants, especially the host responses to Agrobacterium infection and its associated factors. We used RNA-seq to follow the time course of gene expression in Arabidopsis seedlings infected with either avirulent or virulent strains of Agrobacterium. GO (gene ontology) analysis indicated many biological processes were involved in the Agrobacterium-mediated transformation process, including hormone signaling, defense response, cellular biosynthesis, and nucleic acid metabolism. RNA-seq and qRT-PCR results indicated that expression of genes involved in host plant growth and development were repressed but those involved in defense response were induced by Agrobacterium. Further analysis of the responses of transgenic Arabidopsis lines constitutively expressing either the VirE2 or VirE3 proteins suggested Vir proteins act to enhance plant defense responses in addition to their known roles facilitating T-DNA transformation.
